custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create two active parts for this test, part A and part B.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in tab 1 on the Inventory page, on the Active tab.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425781-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425781-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • Theme: click your avatar (the AS circle) at the top right; Light and Dark are at the bottom of its menu.
  • Second tab: open a new browser tab on the same QA site address (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com); you stay signed in as the same user.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A and B are listed.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 4:

  • The part A row is ticked.

Step 5:

  • The bar reads 2 selected.

Step 6:

  • A second tab opens.

Step 7:

  • Tab 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 8:

  • Tab 2 shows the Inventory page.

Step 9:

  • Parts A and B are listed in tab 2.

Step 10:

  • The menu opens in tab 2.

Step 11:

  • Bulk mode turns on in tab 2.

Step 12:

  • The part A row is ticked in tab 2.

Step 13:

  • Tab 2's bar reads 2 selected.

Step 14:

  • The confirmation opens in tab 2.

Step 15:

  • Tab 2 shows "2 parts updated.": parts A and B are now inactive.

Step 16:

  • Tab 1 still shows parts A and B ticked.

Step 17:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 18:

  • A red message reads "No parts were changed." and lists parts A and B, each with "Part is already in that state."
  • The list stays on screen, bulk mode stays on and both parts are still ticked (the bar reads 2 selected), ready to retry.

Step 19:

  • The red message is still on screen after 10 seconds: it stays until closed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S10-N2: “If every part in a bulk change fails, the list stays on screen and the selection is kept, so the user can retry.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Bulk change, every part failed | "No parts were changed." | Error toast, stays until closed, lists each failed part and its reason”
  • User Feedback Summary: “A part already in the requested state | "Part is already in that state." | Listed as the failure reason”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.
